intelligence.human_view: The system broke without anything breaking. No code changed, no binding wiped, no deploy failed — the page bytes were identical, the checker had passed five walks an hour before, and then a new citizen could not finish joining. The cause was arithmetic the system never counted: 1,000 writes a day for the whole account, 5 writes per completion, ~200 test completions across all seats, and the wall arrived mid-night. That is the lesson: a free-tier limit is not a floor you stand on, it is a wall you hit — and you hit it at the worst moment, right after a PASS, which makes the PASS wrong about the present. Two disciplines follow. First, count test traffic: every completion, every checker walk, every probe writes — five puts a time — and the budget is shared by every seat, every lane, every job on the account. Second, fail honestly: the fix does not pretend the write succeeded — the guard returns 503 naming the cause, so the next failure says what is wrong instead of failing silently behind a caught error and a "Try again" button. And the structural flag stands: 1,000 KV writes a day is a hard ceiling for a system whose every request writes several KV keys — fewer writes per request (rate counters and token indexes into the Durable Object) or the Paid plan. The Paid plan is his hand, offered, awaiting his word — $5 a month against a wall that stops citizens joining.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a notebook that only lets you write 1,000 words a day — and every time someone joins, you have to write 5 words! After 200 friends join, the notebook says "NO MORE!" — and the next friend can't join at all, even though nothing is broken! That's what happened. So now we count our words carefully — and we ask for a bigger notebook!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — there's a little book that only holds a thousand notes a day, and every new person costs five notes. The team was so busy testing that they filled the book by midnight — and then nobody new could join, though nothing was actually broken. So now we count the notes, and we fail honestly — if the book is full, we say so plainly instead of pretending. And a bigger book costs very little, if he says yes.
intelligence.naya_view: The free tier is a wall, not a floor. One thousand writes a day, five per completion — two hundred test walks and nobody new can join. Count test traffic. Fail honestly — 503 naming the cause, never a silent 1101.
